When checked, the optical permittivity tensor loaded from the DFT output is
averaged over all point-group symmetry operations of the crystal:
  ε_sym[i,j] = (1/N) Σ_R  R[i,a] R[j,b] ε[a,b]
This projects the raw tensor onto the invariant subspace of the crystal
symmetry, removing numerical noise that violates the lattice symmetry
(e.g. spurious in-plane birefringence in a uniaxial crystal).
Disable only if you need to use the raw, unsymmetrised DFT tensor.

Non-analytical correction (NAC) options.
When enabled, LO frequencies are computed from the dynamical matrix
with the long-range Coulomb correction at the given phonon wavevector q̂.
Applies to both IR and Raman mode tables.

Composite Gauss-Legendre integration point density (points per µm of layer thickness).
20–60 pts/µm is recommended for accuracy.
The actual number of points is density × layer thickness, clamped to [5, 1 000 000].

Incident laser polarisation (p = in the plane of incidence, s = perpendicular).
'porto' means the value was set by the Porto notation entry.

Detected polarisation (p, s, or 'unpolarised' for no analyser; sums |A_p|^2 + |A_s|^2).
'porto' means the value was set by the Porto notation entry.

Apply normal-incidence Porto notation. This sets the crystal hkl direction, incident/detected polarisation, normal incidence, and collection side.
Propagation signs: same signs mean forward scattering, so the detector is on the substrate side; opposite signs mean backscattering, so the detector is on the superstrate/incident side.
A bare final direction is treated as the common backscattering shorthand: x(yy)x is equivalent to x(yy)-x, and -x(yy)x is also backscattering.
Examples: x(yy)x = backscattering, y-in/y-out; x(yz)-x = backscattering, y-in/z-out; x(yz)+x = forward scattering.
Use comma-separated compound polarisations for mixed directions, for example z(x+y,x+y)z for linear polarisation along the in-plane x+y direction. Compound Porto polarisations override the p/s combo-box selections; after Apply the combos show 'porto' to indicate that the Porto entry is controlling them.

Apply normal-incidence Porto notation. This sets the crystal hkl direction, incident/detected polarisation, normal incidence, and collection side.
Propagation signs: same signs mean forward scattering, so the detector is on the substrate side; opposite signs mean backscattering, so the detector is on the superstrate/incident side.

Which side the detector is on:
'superstrate' = backscattering (default)
'substrate' = forward scattering (reversed stack for E_S)

Collection (detector) angle in degrees.
−1 = automatic: retro-backscattering from the superstrate side or collinear forward scattering from the substrate side.
Set an explicit angle equal to the incidence angle for specular reflection.

How Raman sources are combined through the depth of each active layer:
'Coherent amplitude' integrates the complex amplitude before squaring; use for thin phase-stable films.
'Incoherent intensity' integrates local intensity; use for thick or bulk samples such as mm/cm layers.
Note: 'Incoherent intensity' also forces incoherent layer combination.

How separate Raman-active layers are combined:
'Incoherent intensities' — sum |amplitude|² per layer (default).
'Coherent amplitudes' — sum complex amplitudes before squaring;
   use only when layers share a coherent optical phase.
Disabled when 'Depth coherence' is 'Incoherent intensity'.
Include the electro-optic χ⁽²⁾ contribution in NAC-corrected Raman tensors when χ⁽²⁾ is available.

Layer NAC mode — phonon frequency correction for layered crystal Raman:
'TO' — use bulk TO frequencies (no correction)
'Snell's law' — NAC q from macroscopic scattering geometry
'Dominant mode' — NAC q from dominant Berreman eigenmode in the active layer
'All modes' — per Berreman mode-pair NAC: sums |A^ij|² over (i_L, j_S) pairs
Labels show '(EO)' when χ⁽²⁾ is available and the electro-optic term is enabled.

'Coherent amplitude' integrates the complex amplitude before squaring; use for thin phase-stable films.

Layer NAC mode — phonon frequency correction for layered crystal Raman:
'TO' — use bulk TO frequencies (no correction)
'Snell's law' — NAC q from macroscopic scattering geometry
'Dominant mode' — NAC q from dominant Berreman eigenmode in the active layer
'All modes' — per Berreman mode-pair NAC: sums |A^ij|² over (i_L, j_S) pairs
Labels show '(EO)' when χ⁽²⁾ is available and the electro-optic term is enabled.

How Berreman modal-pair amplitudes are combined (only active when Layer NAC mode = All modes):
'Group q channels' — coherently sum pairs that share the same phonon q-vector
   and detector channel. Physically recommended.
'Incoherent pairs' — square each modal-pair amplitude independently.
   Diagnostic / pre-q-grouping compatibility mode.
'Coherent all pairs' — sum ALL pair amplitudes before squaring. DEBUG ONLY:
   mixes distinct phonon-momentum final states.

How internal Berreman pairs map to phonon final states when depth is incoherent:
'Bulk phase matched' compares each internal q_pair with q_ext; the q-angle tolerance selects the accepted forward momentum hemisphere.
'Local incoherent' assigns all local optical-field components to the externally selected state; q-angle filtering is not used.

Maximum angle between an internal q_pair and the external momentum transfer q_ext
in the bulk phase-matched model. 90° accepts the forward momentum hemisphere
and rejects antiparallel pairs. This setting is inactive for local incoherent depth.

controls.text:
COORDINATE SYSTEM
─────────────────
Three directions in crystal coordinates define the geometry:

1. The light propagation direction Rz.

2. The direction Pz showing the laser polarisation direction at zero-angle.
   This should be perpendicular to Rz. 
   When Rz is changed orthogonality of Pz is ensured automatically. 
   Pza can also be changed, but orthogonality is not enforces
   'Orthogonality' displays the orthogonality between Pz and Rz
3. The remaining orthogonal direct Pp = Rz × Pz

PLOT LEGEND
───────────────
The sample is rotated by angle θ (via rotation matrix M):

• VV (vertical-vertical / parallel)
    Both incident and scattered polarisations rotate together.
    E_L = M·Pz,  E_S = M·Pz

• HV (horizontal-vertical / perpendicular)
    Incident and scattered polarisations are always perpendicular;
    both rotate with the sample — equivalent to simultaneous
    rotation around Pz and Pp.
    E_L = M·Pza,  E_S = M·Pp

• Theta (fixed incident, rotating analyser)
    Incident polarisation is fixed; the analyser rotates.
    E_L = Pz  (fixed),  E_S = M·Pz

REFERENCE
─────────
This visualisation is inspired by the CRD/Oulu Raman simulator.
https://ramandb.oulu.fi/simulator 
Please cite:
M. Bagheri and H.-P. Komsa, 
 "High-throughput computation of Raman spectra from first principles"
 Scientific Data 10, 80 (2023).
https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-023-01988-5
